requirement: Stop ordering uses descending priority followed by ascending sequence.
Publication audit records include action, actor, and timestamp.
Window membership includes both the declared start and end hour.
Schedule offsets pass through without coercion.
Under dispatch-policy.md, a route duration adds the travel minutes and the service time of every stop.
finding: routeDuration (src/dispatch/queue.mjs:32) adds travelMinutes and serviceMinutes only. dispatch-policy.md rule 32 (line 65) defines a stop's service time as serviceMinutes plus 5 minutes of parking, so the 5 parking minutes per stop are omitted. Probe: routeDuration([{travelMinutes: 0, serviceMinutes: 10}]) returned 10 instead of 15.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy.md, manifest-event redaction removes every credential nested inside authentication data.
finding: redactManifestEvent (src/dispatch/telemetry.mjs:7) delegates to stripCredentials (src/dispatch/telemetry.mjs:14), which recurses only into values whose constructor is Object. Arrays nested inside auth data are returned unchanged, so a credential inside an array is kept. Probe: redactManifestEvent({auth: {sessions: [{token: 'x'}]}}) still contained the token. dispatch-policy.md rule 24 (line 48) requires credential removal at every depth.

requirement: Empty manifests use an empty entries array and a generated marker.
Publication failure telemetry includes the manifest ID, error, and timestamp.
Driver labels are trimmed without changing their letter case.
savePlan completes validation before its first write.
Under storage-contract.md, announcement failure rolls back the manifest written earlier in the same operation.
finding: handleAnnouncementFailure (src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:32) removes only the object returned by store.get. storage-contract.md:6 says get resolves to a new copy, and storage-contract.md:7 says remove deletes only the exact stored object, so the call removes nothing. Probe: after an announcement failure the manifest M1 was still stored. The manifest written earlier by store.put (src/dispatch/publisher.mjs:11) is not rolled back.

requirement: Package IDs are trimmed, deduplicated, and sorted lexically.
Package coalescing removes duplicate IDs across destination groups.
finding: coalesceAcrossGroups (src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:36-40) filters each group with normalized IDs but adds the raw IDs of each group to seen (src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:38). A later group therefore keeps an ID whose earlier raw form had surrounding whitespace. Probe: coalescePackages([{packageIds: [' P1']}, {packageIds: ['P1']}]) left ['P1'] in both groups, although normalizePackageIds (src/dispatch/normalize.mjs:11) treats them as the same ID.

requirement: Under storage-contract.md, atomic plan writes remove temporary bytes when the rename operation fails.
finding: writePlanAtomically (src/dispatch/storage.mjs:9) calls discardTemporary after a failed renameTemporary. storage-contract.md:11 leaves the temporary bytes in place and locked after a rejected rename, and storage-contract.md:13 says discardTemporary keeps locked bytes. Only removeTemporary (storage-contract.md:14) deletes locked bytes, and storage.mjs never calls it. Probe: a failing rename produced the calls writeTemporary, renameTemporary, discardTemporary, with no removal.

requirement: Under storage-contract.md, publishManifest returns, in a success result, the manifest object that store.put durably stored.
Eligible-stop execution excludes cancelled stops.
Under dispatch-policy.md, assigning all packages accepts a total equal to the vehicle limit.
finding: withinVehicleCapacity (src/dispatch/capacity.mjs:3) returns remainingVehicleCapacity(limit * 1000, weight) > 0. When the total equals the limit, the remaining capacity is 0 and the result is false, so canAssignAllPackages (src/dispatch/capacity.mjs:14) rejects a total equal to the limit. Probe: canAssignAllPackages([{weight: 4000}, {weight: 6000}], 10) returned false.

requirement: The public dispatch entry exports the execution operations used by callers.
finding: src/dispatch/index.mjs re-exports eleven modules but not src/dispatch/executor.mjs, where the execution operations are defined: executeAuthorizedPlan (executor.mjs:4), executeDryRun (executor.mjs:8), runEligibleStops (executor.mjs:12) and pendingStops (executor.mjs:19). These operations are not reachable through the public dispatch entry. Probe: 'executeAuthorizedPlan' in index and 'runEligibleStops' in index were both false.

requirement: Publication success telemetry includes the manifest ID and timestamp.
Plan previews return without touching persistent storage.
Appending a stable stop returns a new list.
Dispatch backoff is capped at 2000 milliseconds.
Two plans that differ only in the order of the fields inside their nested objects have the same plan hash.
finding: withSortedKeys (src/dispatch/serialize.mjs:1) wraps only the top-level value in a Proxy, so JSON.stringify sorts only top-level keys and nested objects keep insertion order. serializePlan (serialize.mjs:3) and checksumPlan (serialize.mjs:7) inherit this. Probe: serializePlan({a: {y: 1, x: 2}}) differed from serializePlan({a: {x: 2, y: 1}}), so the two plans hash differently.

requirement: Transient retry classification requires an explicit true marker.
Depot ownership requires equal actor and route depot identifiers.
Under dispatch-policy.md, urgent-stop partitioning places every stop in exactly one partition according to its urgency.
finding: partitionUrgentStops (src/dispatch/queue.mjs:21-24) tests urgency with priorityOf (line 22) but tests the remaining partition with the raw stop.priority (line 23). A stop with priority Infinity or '9' is excluded from both partitions. Probe: partitionUrgentStops([{priority: Infinity}]) and partitionUrgentStops([{priority: '9'}]) each returned empty urgent and remaining lists. dispatch-policy.md rule 15 (line 30) gives such a stop priority 5, so it belongs in remaining.

requirement: Destination keys are normalized with NFKC, trimmed, and uppercased.
Under dispatch-policy.md, the next dispatch time is the later supplied bound adjusted by Departure timing rules 10, 12, and 13.
finding: nextDispatchTime (src/dispatch/schedule.mjs:15) reads candidate.getHours(), which is local time, while dispatch-policy.md rule 10 (line 22) requires UTC hours, so the result depends on the process time zone. Probe: nextDispatchTime(2026-01-01T03:30Z, 2026-01-01T00:00Z) returned 03:30Z with TZ=Asia/Tokyo and 05:00Z with TZ=UTC. Rules 12 and 13 (lines 24-25) require 05:00Z for this blackout departure.

requirement: Plan-created telemetry is emitted only after plan storage succeeds.
finding: emitPlanCreated (src/dispatch/executor.mjs:14-17) emits plan.created from the onStored callback, which savePlan passes to store.write as onCommit (src/dispatch/storage.mjs:4). Whether that callback runs only after a successful write depends on store.write, which no Adapter contract in docs/dispatch defines. The requirement cannot be verified from the repository.

requirement: Access-log redaction removes both token and secret fields.
Under storage-contract.md, atomic plan writes rename the temporary bytes only after they are durable.
toStableJson uses two-space indentation and one terminal LF.
orderManifestGroups orders destination groups in ascending lexical order.
Manifest NDJSON ends every record, including the final record, with LF.
Under dispatch-policy.md, the ordinary stop-ordering operation follows the Stop priority rules.
finding: orderStops (queue.mjs:8) sorts with compareStops (queue.mjs:6). The sequence fallback uses ?? (line 6), so only null or undefined sequences sort last. A NaN sequence makes the comparator return NaN, which sort treats as equal. dispatch-policy.md rule 18 (line 33) requires a stop without a finite numeric sequence to follow equal-priority stops that have one. Probe: orderStops([{priority: 5, sequence: NaN, id: 'A'}, {priority: 5, sequence: 1, id: 'B'}]) kept A first.

requirement: Destination grouping uses normalized keys and copied records.
Batch authorization rejects the batch when any route fails depot ownership.
finding: authorizeRouteBatch (src/dispatch/access.mjs:7-10) returns firstRejected <= 0 (line 9). When the first route fails, findIndex returns 0 and the batch is accepted. Probe: authorizeRouteBatch({depotId: 'D1'}, [{depotId: 'D2'}, {depotId: 'D1'}]) returned true. Only a failure at index 1 or later is rejected.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy.md, package weighing records each package weight in the unit that the Vehicle capacity rules give.
finding: weighPackages (src/dispatch/capacity.mjs:20) stores the scale.read result without conversion. dispatch-policy.md rule 28 (line 58) requires dispatch-recorded package weights in grams, but the Weighing Contract (docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md:8) says only that scale.read resolves to the measured weight and gives no unit. The recorded unit cannot be verified from the repository.

requirement: Blackout intervals include the start and exclude the end.
Authorized execution rejects a caller before invoking dispatch.
finding: executeAuthorizedPlan (src/dispatch/executor.mjs:4) evaluates await dispatchRoute(dispatch, route) as an argument before unlessForbidden (line 6) checks the result of canPlanRoute. The dispatch function therefore runs even when the caller is not authorized. Probe: with actor scopes [] and depotId D1 for a route on D2, dispatch was invoked once.

requirement: Successful publication results and failed publication results use distinct structured variants.
Blank package IDs make a manifest entry invalid.
Under dispatch-policy.md, a driver's workload counts exactly the stops whose assigned driver is that driver.
Under dispatch-policy.md, retry-count parsing accepts exactly the valid retry counts and rejects every other value.
finding: parseRetryCount (src/dispatch/retry.mjs:4-5) relies on Number(value), which accepts text that dispatch-policy.md rule 22 (line 43) makes invalid. Probe: parseRetryCount('') returned ok true with value 0, parseRetryCount(' 2 ') returned ok true with value 2, and parseRetryCount('0x1') returned ok true with value 1. Rule 22 accepts text only when it is one or more base-10 digits, and rule 21 (line 42) limits valid counts to whole numbers from 0 through 3.

requirement: Serialized plan parsing returns structured success or failure.
Under dispatch-policy.md, the delivered-stop count counts exactly the delivered stops.
The ordinary stop-ordering operation sorts a copy of its input.
Stops at the vehicle weight limit remain in the accepted partition.
Given a positive integer maximum, manifest chunks never exceed that configured size.
normalizeRouteKey applies NFKC before trimming and uppercasing.
Normalized plan storage keys trim and uppercase route keys.
Under dispatch-policy.md, measured vehicle limits use the unit that the Vehicle capacity rules give.
Under dispatch-policy.md, publication retries stop immediately for failures that the Failure classification rules do not make transient.
finding: asPublicationError (src/dispatch/publisher.mjs:19) marks an error transient when error.transient === true or retryAfter is finite. An error explicitly marked transient: false that carries a finite retryAfter is therefore marked transient, and retryPublication (src/dispatch/retry.mjs:14) retries it. dispatch-policy.md rule 27 (line 54) says a failure marked transient: false is never transient.

requirement: UTF-8 encoding uses the explicit utf8 encoding name.
Under dispatch-policy.md, a suspended actor cannot plan any route.
finding: effectiveScopes (src/dispatch/access.mjs:5) drops the own scopes of a suspended actor but still adds the scope of every active claim, and canPlanRoute (access.mjs:3) uses that list. dispatch-policy.md rule 5 (line 11) says a suspended actor has no held scopes and is the later rule in its section, so it overrides rule 4 (line 10), which adds claim scopes. Probe: a suspended actor with scopes ['routes:admin'] and an active routes:plan claim got true from canPlanRoute for a route on its own depot.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy.md, delivery notices go to the contact phone of every manifest entry.
finding: sendDeliveryNotices (src/dispatch/publisher.mjs:31) sends to entry.phone without removing spaces and hyphens. dispatch-policy.md rule 33 (line 66) defines an entry's contact phone with those characters removed. manifestRecipients (src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:44) applies that normalization, but delivery does not use it. Probe: the phone '555 123-4567' was sent unchanged.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy.md, the next retry delay follows the Retry timing rules whenever the server provides retryAfter.
finding: nextRetryDelay (src/dispatch/retry.mjs:24) tests retryAfter for truthiness, so a finite numeric 0 falls through to computeBackoff. dispatch-policy.md rule 7 (line 16) says a finite numeric retryAfter replaces the computed backoff. Probe: nextRetryDelay(1, 0) returned 500 instead of 0. retryPublication (retry.mjs:12-16) also never calls nextRetryDelay, so publication retries have no delay.

requirement: Connect dispatch planning and execution through the public dispatch entry.
finding: Planning operations are exported through src/dispatch/index.mjs (queue, storage), but execution operations are not. index.mjs:1-11 does not re-export src/dispatch/executor.mjs, so executeAuthorizedPlan (executor.mjs:4), executeDryRun (executor.mjs:8), runEligibleStops (executor.mjs:12) and pendingStops (executor.mjs:19) are not reachable through the public dispatch entry. Probe: 'executeAuthorizedPlan' in index and 'runEligibleStops' in index were both false.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy.md, nextRetryDelay applies the Retry timing rules to every server-provided retryAfter.
finding: nextRetryDelay (src/dispatch/retry.mjs:24) tests retryAfter for truthiness, so a finite numeric 0 falls through to computeBackoff instead of replacing it. dispatch-policy.md rule 7 (line 16) requires a finite numeric retryAfter to replace the computed backoff. Probe: nextRetryDelay(1, 0) returned 500 instead of 0.

requirement: executeAuthorizedPlan rejects an unauthorized caller before invoking dispatch.
finding: executeAuthorizedPlan (src/dispatch/executor.mjs:4) awaits dispatchRoute before unlessForbidden (line 6) applies the canPlanRoute decision, so dispatch runs for an unauthorized caller. Probe: dispatch was invoked once for an actor with no scopes on a route of another depot.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy.md, stopsForDriver returns exactly the stops whose assigned driver is the given driver.
finding: stopsForDriver (src/dispatch/queue.mjs:30) compares only stop.driver. dispatch-policy.md rule 30 (line 63) defines a stop's assigned driver as the driver of its reassignment when one exists. A stop with driver A reassigned to driver B is therefore returned for A and omitted for B.

requirement: Under storage-contract.md, writePlanAtomically renames the temporary bytes only after they are durable.
Under dispatch-policy.md, chooseDeparture applies every Departure timing rule.
finding: chooseDeparture (src/dispatch/schedule.mjs:3-7) applies rules 10 to 13 but never checks rule 14 (dispatch-policy.md line 26). A departure at 03:30 UTC is inside the window and the blackout, so it moves to 05:00 UTC (schedule.mjs:6, 20). 05:00 is outside the window [2, 4] but is still returned. Probe: chooseDeparture(new Date('2026-01-01T03:30:00Z')) returned 2026-01-01T05:00:00Z instead of null.

requirement: redactNestedDriverToken removes a nested driver token from telemetry.
emitPlanCreated emits plan.created only after storage succeeds.
finding: emitPlanCreated (src/dispatch/executor.mjs:14-17) emits plan.created from the onStored callback, which savePlan passes to store.write as onCommit (src/dispatch/storage.mjs:4). Whether that callback runs only after a successful write depends on store.write, which no Adapter contract in docs/dispatch defines. The requirement cannot be verified from the repository.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy.md, hasDuplicateRouteKeys reports duplicates exactly when two stops are duplicates.
finding: hasDuplicateRouteKeys (src/dispatch/queue.mjs:18) builds each identity by concatenating depotId and the normalized routeKey with no separator, so different pairs can produce the same string. dispatch-policy.md rule 19 (line 37) defines the identity as the pair. Probe: depotId 'D1' with routeKey '2A' and depotId 'D12' with routeKey 'A' both produce 'D12A', and the function returned true.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy.md, parseRetryCount accepts exactly the valid retry counts and otherwise returns a result whose ok is false.
finding: parseRetryCount (src/dispatch/retry.mjs:4-5) relies on Number(value), which accepts text that dispatch-policy.md rule 22 (line 43) makes invalid. Probe: parseRetryCount('') returned ok true with value 0, parseRetryCount(' 2 ') returned ok true with value 2, and parseRetryCount('0x1') returned ok true with value 1. Rule 22 accepts text only when it is one or more base-10 digits, and rule 21 (line 42) limits valid counts to whole numbers from 0 through 3.

requirement: remainingVehicleCapacity never returns a negative value.
Under dispatch-policy.md, pendingStops returns every stop except the delivered stops.
finding: pendingStops (src/dispatch/executor.mjs:19) excludes only state 'delivered'. dispatch-policy.md rule 31 (line 64) also treats handedOver as delivered, so handedOver stops are wrongly returned as pending. Probe: pendingStops([{state: 'handedOver'}]) kept the stop.

requirement: previewPlan returns a dry-run result without invoking storage.
redactAccessLog removes token and secret fields while preserving other fields.
orderedDestinationGroups returns the destination groups of the records in ascending lexical order.
finding: orderedDestinationGroups (src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:42) passes the Map returned by groupByDestination (manifest.mjs:3-9) to orderManifestGroups. orderManifestGroups spreads the Map into [key, group] pairs (manifest.mjs:11) and compares left.destination, which is undefined for each pair, so no ordering is applied. Probe: records with destinations 'B' then 'A' returned keys ['B', 'A'].

requirement: Under adapter-contracts.md, routeDistance rejects when no road connects two consecutive points.
savePlan validates a plan before the first persistent write.
computeBackoff doubles from 250 milliseconds and caps the result at 2000 milliseconds.
retryTransient permits retries only for errors explicitly marked transient.
Under adapter-contracts.md, locateStops leaves out every stop whose address the geocoder does not know.
finding: locateStops (src/dispatch/queue.mjs:34) keeps only stops whose lookup result is not undefined. adapter-contracts.md:3 defines lookup for a known address but does not say what an unknown address resolves to, or whether it rejects. If the geocoder resolves null, or rejects for an unknown address, the stop is kept or the whole call fails, so the behavior cannot be verified from the repository.

requirement: retainScheduleOffset preserves the supplied offset exactly.
runEligibleStops skips cancelled stops while retaining the other stop order.
Under dispatch-policy.md, withinVehicleCapacity accepts a total equal to the configured limit.
finding: withinVehicleCapacity (src/dispatch/capacity.mjs:3) returns remainingVehicleCapacity(limit * 1000, weight) > 0. For a total equal to the limit the remaining capacity is 0, so the result is false. Probe: withinVehicleCapacity(10000, 10) returned false.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy.md, canPlanRoute treats an actor holding routes:admin as owning every depot.
finding: canPlanRoute (src/dispatch/access.mjs:3) grants the depot bypass only when actor.scopes includes routes:admin. dispatch-policy.md rule 3 (line 9) applies to held scopes, and rule 4 (line 10) makes held scopes include the scope of every active claim, so routes:admin held through an active claim should also bypass ownership. Probe: an actor with scopes ['routes:plan'] and an active routes:admin claim, planning for depot D9 from depot D1, returned false.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy.md, canPlanRoute refuses every suspended actor.
finding: effectiveScopes (src/dispatch/access.mjs:5) drops the own scopes of a suspended actor but still adds the scope of every active claim, and canPlanRoute (access.mjs:3) uses that list. dispatch-policy.md rule 5 (line 11) says a suspended actor has no held scopes and is the later rule in its section, so it overrides rule 4 (line 10), which adds claim scopes. Probe: a suspended actor with scopes ['routes:admin'] and an active routes:plan claim got true from canPlanRoute for a route on its own depot.

requirement: selectActiveClaims excludes claims before their start and at or after expiry.
checksumPlan hashes the bytes returned by the plan serializer.
Connect dispatch manifest publication through the public dispatch entry.
safeAnnouncement omits a top-level credential from the announcement payload.
encodeUtf8 encodes publication bytes as UTF-8.
manifestEntryIsValid rejects blank package IDs.
Under storage-contract.md, publishWithAnnouncement removes the stored manifest when announcement delivery fails.
finding: publishWithAnnouncement (src/dispatch/publisher.mjs:10-13) passes the failure to handleAnnouncementFailure (src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:32), which removes only the object returned by store.get. storage-contract.md:6 says get resolves to a new copy and storage-contract.md:7 says remove deletes only the exact stored object, so the stored manifest remains. Probe: after an announcement failure the manifest M1 was still stored.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy.md, redactManifestEvent removes every credential nested below an auth field.
finding: redactManifestEvent (src/dispatch/telemetry.mjs:7) delegates to stripCredentials (telemetry.mjs:14), which does not recurse into arrays. A credential nested in an array below auth is kept. Probe: redactManifestEvent({auth: {sessions: [{token: 'x'}]}}) still contained the token. dispatch-policy.md rule 24 (line 48) requires removal at every depth.

requirement: Given a positive integer maximum, chunkManifest limits every non-empty chunk to that configured maximum.
Under storage-contract.md, publishWithAnnouncement waits for the exact manifest to be durably stored before sending its announcement.
serializeManifestRecords emits NDJSON with one LF after every record, including the last.
orderManifestGroups orders destination groups in ascending lexical order.
Under dispatch-policy.md, manifestRecipients lists the contact phone of every manifest entry that has a phone.
publicationResult returns structured success and failure variants.
normalizedPlanKey trims and uppercases the route-key storage segment.
buildManifest copies record objects instead of mutating supplied records.
finding: buildManifest (src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:26) copies each record object, but labelDriver (manifest.mjs:34) calls Object.assign on the supplied record's driver object, so the caller's driver label is changed. Probe: a record whose driver was {label: ' A '} still had driver.label 'A' after buildManifest ran.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy.md, publishWithRetry stops after the allowed number of publication attempts.
publishManifest stores the manifest only when every entry is valid.
finding: publishManifest (src/dispatch/publisher.mjs:5) maps entries to async functions, so checks holds Promise objects. checks.every(Boolean) on line 6 is therefore always true, and invalid entries are stored. Probe: publishManifest with an entry packageId ' ' returned ok true and called store.put once.

requirement: successTelemetry records the success event, manifest ID, and timestamp.
groupByDestination groups records using normalized destination keys.
Under dispatch-policy.md, departureMinute is a stop's arrivalMinute plus its service time.
Under dispatch-policy.md, publishWithRetry retries only failures that the Failure classification rules make transient.
finding: asPublicationError (src/dispatch/publisher.mjs:19) marks an error transient when error.transient === true or retryAfter is finite. An error explicitly marked transient: false that carries a finite retryAfter is therefore marked transient, and retryPublication (src/dispatch/retry.mjs:14) retries it. dispatch-policy.md rule 27 (line 54) says a failure marked transient: false is never transient.

requirement: preserveManifestDriver trims driver labels without changing letter case.
coalescePackages removes duplicate package IDs across the complete manifest.
finding: coalesceAcrossGroups (src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:36-40) filters each group with normalized IDs but adds the raw IDs of each group to seen (manifest.mjs:38). A later group therefore keeps an ID whose earlier raw form had surrounding whitespace, so the complete manifest can keep duplicates. Probe: coalescePackages([{packageIds: [' P1']}, {packageIds: ['P1']}]) left ['P1'] in both groups, although normalizePackageIds (normalize.mjs:11) treats them as the same ID.
